appearance.bark_look.stages.blackjack.note: until_diameter_m: text: 'Younger trees, up to 2 feet in diameter ... blackish, narrowly furrowed' (Sudworth); fissures.width_share: word: 'narrowly furrowed'; fissures.spacing_m: inferred (photo)

appearance.bark_look.stages.plates.colou.note: text: 'yellow to orange-red', 'russet-red' (Wikipedia, Sudworth); sRGB by eye

appearance.bark_look.stages.plates.note: fissures.network: text: 'cross-checked into broadly rectangular, scaly plates' (FNA); fissures.spacing_m: word: 'very broad, shield-like' plates (Sudworth); size inferred (photo); scales: text: 'made up of small, concave scales' (Sudworth); size inferred under Junikka's 7.5 cm

generator.params.pipe_tip.note: Farjon's Pinus ponderosa account (printed pp. 761-763): new shoots 0.7 to 2 cm thick. The twig behind each living apex is drawn 0.8 cm thick, near the thin end of the range, as shaded shoots are thinner; with the crown shading by its needles' own area (generator revision 85) it carries four times the shoots, and 1 cm twigs then made a 60-year trunk 62 cm across.

generator.params.pipe_organ.note: A choice of the model's (pinidae revision 11): the pipe radius each metre of needle tuft adds, raised from 0.012 to 0.028 (for a spray bearing 0.25 m² a metre squared; the program scales it by each spray's own leaf area) with pipe_tip so the limbs carrying ponderosa's stout shoots and heavy tufts of 15 to 25 cm needles (Farjon 2017, pp. 761-763) hold their line at 100 years. Farjon describes the branches as spreading and assurgent, the lower ones curved down or somewhat pendulous, which the old crown keeps; with the old values they hung as whips to the ground.

generator.params.pipe_exponent.note: A choice of the model's (pinidae revision 11): 3 in place of 2.4, so the stout limbs above do not also thicken the trunk; diameter at breast height stays near the old values (about 32 cm at 30 years, 39 cm at 100) inside the 60-year reference's tolerance.

traits.self_pruning.note: FEIS's ponderosa pine review (Pinus ponderosa var. ponderosa, PDF read): "Ponderosa pine tends to self-prune, although some open-grown trees on unburned sites may have branches nearly reaching the ground"; its adaptations to fire include a high, open crown and self- and fire-pruned branches.

traits.height_max_m.note: Silvics vol. 1 (1990), Ponderosa Pine chapter: heights of 27.4 to 39.6 m (90 to 130 ft) are common through most of the range; a record of 70.7 m has been measured.

traits.wood_modulus_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Pine, ponderosa, green: modulus of elasticity 6,900 MPa in static bending (clear wood, centre-loaded, span 14 depths; specific gravity 0.38).

traits.wood_rupture_green_mpa.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 5-3a, Pine, ponderosa, green: modulus of rupture 35,000 kPa (clear wood in static bending).

traits.wood_moisture_green_share.note: Wood Handbook 2021 (FPL-GTR-282), table 4-1, Pine, ponderosa: average moisture content of green wood, heartwood 40% and sapwood 148% of oven-dry mass; stated as a share, the range between them with its middle typical where both are given.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Pinus ponderosa (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.42 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 32 records in 8 sources); trunks 0.41, branches 0.45. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.leaf_life_years.note: FEIS's ponderosa pine review: needles kept three or four years and shed in autumn; Abrams gives about three.

traits.needles_per_fascicle.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 56): needles in threes (sometimes twos), 12 to 25 cm, in dense tufts at the branch ends, kept about three years; seed cones 7 to 15 cm, short-stalked, set horizontally or bent somewhat down, shedding seed in their second year and soon falling.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 56): needles in threes (sometimes twos), 12 to 25 cm, in dense tufts at the branch ends, kept about three years; seed cones 7 to 15 cm, short-stalked, set horizontally or bent somewhat down, shedding seed in their second year and soon falling.

traits.cone_length_m.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 56): needles in threes (sometimes twos), 12 to 25 cm, in dense tufts at the branch ends, kept about three years; seed cones 7 to 15 cm, short-stalked, set horizontally or bent somewhat down, shedding seed in their second year and soon falling. Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 476: seed cones (5-)7-12(-15) cm. The spec stated {"min": 0.07, "max": 0.15}. Combined on the owner's rule (2026-10-15): where two sources differ, both are kept and the range spans them.

traits.cone_posture.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 56): needles in threes (sometimes twos), 12 to 25 cm, in dense tufts at the branch ends, kept about three years; seed cones 7 to 15 cm, short-stalked, set horizontally or bent somewhat down, shedding seed in their second year and soon falling.

traits.cone_retention_years.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 56): needles in threes (sometimes twos), 12 to 25 cm, in dense tufts at the branch ends, kept about three years; seed cones 7 to 15 cm, short-stalked, set horizontally or bent somewhat down, shedding seed in their second year and soon falling.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS (Fryer 2018, read): ponderosa pine first produces seeds at 10 to 20 years old, sometimes as early as 7. The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Pinus, table 2, read): seed bearing begins at 16 to 20 years in var. ponderosa, 6 to 20 in var. scopulorum. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 15 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a large pine with an open, rounded crown, stout branches and long needles in bundles of three, tufted at the twig ends. Not fitted to measurements. Cones (plant forms F3): 8 to 14 cm, spreading to hanging; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spray area (plant roadmap P4): the area its card draws now that its needles stand in fascicles. Spec rework E6d: `cone_length`, `cone_years`, `cone_pitch`, `needle_years` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated characters. Conifer form (pinidae revision 5): `branch_reach` fitted so the open-grown crown keeps revision 4's radius at the oldest keyframe, and `pipe_rings` refitted to the dbh references now that the crown holds more foliage; `epi_chance` 0, as pines seldom sprout from dormant buds on their branches (general knowledge, not measured).

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 24 m tall and 50 cm across at breast height at 60 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: yellow-green needles; orange-brown bark in large plates. Needle shoots (plant roadmap P4): needles in threes, 12 to 25 cm long and about 1.5 mm wide, so a needle 0.009 as wide as it is long (`width`), 3 to a fascicle (`bundle`), from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): large cinnamon-orange plates between deep dark fissures on old trees; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `needle`, `bundle`, `ranks` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated needles.
